zh.title: 真正高级的躺平，本质上就两个字
zh.hook: 「找个差不多的工作就能躺」——这是我听过最危险的躺平计划。
zh.body:
差不多的薪资 ≠ 自由度；看起来清闲 ≠ 能摸鱼；低薪 = 最先被裁。
这不叫躺平，叫温水煮青蛙。

真正养人的公司只看一点：结构性的稀缺位置。合规成本高、有战略价值、招人保守、对员工不错——就像伊朗扼守霍尔木兹海峡。

视频里我把识别方法讲清楚了。
zh.cta: 你现在的工作是哪一种？评论区聊聊。

en.cover_title: Real lying flat is one word
en.title: The 'good enough' job is the most dangerous way to lie flat
en.hook: "I'll take a so-so job and coast" is the riskiest career plan I hear from young people.
en.body:
So-so pay ≠ freedom. Looks easy ≠ you can slack. Low pay = first to be cut.
That's not lying flat. That's boiling the frog.

Jobs that actually let you rest sit at structurally scarce positions: expensive to comply, strategically valuable, conservative hiring, decent to staff. Think Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.

In the video I show how to spot them.
en.cta: Which kind is your job? Tell me in the comments.

youtube.title: The 'Good Enough' Job Is the Most Dangerous Way to Lie Flat

linkedin.body:
Talking to early-career folks, I keep hearing the same plan: find a comfortable, average job and coast.

In my experience that plan carries three risks people don't price in:
1. Average pay rarely buys real autonomy.
2. 'Easy' roles leave no energy to build your own edge.
3. Low pay means low security when the cycle turns.

The roles that genuinely let you breathe sit at structurally scarce positions: high compliance cost, strategic value, conservative hiring. Like a strait everyone has to sail through.

Short video below (Chinese with English subtitles).
